done.why: I poked at a handful of rooms and objects, mostly got polite refusals, and stopped well short of any ending.

about: A Zork II style underground empire. You start sealed in a barrow with a lamp and an elvish sword, then move through a cavern, a garden with a unicorn and a gazebo, and a wizard who pops in to cast spells on you.

moments.note: The barrow door has shut behind you and there is no way out. North only gets a flavor line.
The Wizard appeared and cast Fantasize on me. Nothing visibly happened.
The room listed a basilisk, but examining it gave 'You can't see any such thing.' I guessed the Wizard's spell was the cause, but nothing confirmed it.
The unicorn regards the lamp with polite incomprehension, which is a charming reply to an odd offer.
Unusual phrasings such as 'show the basilisk its reflection in the sword' got 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.'

wished: To interact with the basilisk, if it is real or imaginary.
To find out what the unicorn wears around its neck.
To learn what the Wizard's spell did.

lines.line: For a change, you look before leaping. You realize you would never survive.
lines.why: A witty reply to a contrary action.

lines.line: I've known strange people, but fighting a bridge?
lines.why: The world answers my oddness in character.

lines.line: The unicorn regards the lamp with polite incomprehension, and goes back to cropping grass.
lines.why: Charming reply to a silly offer.

fun.why: A few witty refusals, and the Wizard's arrival was a nice surprise. I explored little.

engagement.why: Intriguing hooks like the basilisk and the unicorn's necklace, but I stopped early.

difficulty.why: Nothing blocked me in the short stretch I played. The parser rejected some odd phrasings.

interestingness.why: A faithful Zork II setting with a roaming wizard and a garden.

prose.why: Evocative room descriptions and good humorous refusals.
